caveats: Process-cold startup can use warm OS/project UVM parse artifacts. Initialization, first edit, subsequent edits and fallback stages are separate.
Diagnostic latency ends at matching edited-document-version notification, not whole-workspace diagnostic completion.
Manual rebuild command and post-rebuild edit costs do not include separately untimed instance selection; do not sum them as exact full rebuild latency.
Kernel lifetime peak is physical footprint, not peak RSS; boundary memory is not a process memory ceiling.
Background cases add a small editable consumer; real-edit cases use actual project files and configured stable siblings/packages. Package-only real-edit selections are not full RTL freezing.
Stable API timings are one-process lifecycle observations after mutable consumer diagnostics, not independent repetitions, cold views, percentiles or typing-frequency tails.
Valid awaited body edits do not establish behavior for arbitrary incomplete burst typing.
Experiments remain disabled by default. Correct Native fallback and explicit performance tradeoffs remain part of the supported contract.
Source-history retirement thresholds are independent of unlimited semantic caches. No source-history threshold was lowered to force the long-edit reset.

performanceTradeoffs.method: Differences of current-cohort medians versus Native; positive is higher cost. No weighting across unrelated user workflows and no cross-version latency relabelling. Kernel peak is physical footprint, not peak RSS.
conclusions: Combined local updates give large warm benefits in eligible large designs/UVM consumers. Small real-file always blocks and nonunique module occurrences often use Native local-update fallback; freezing alone can be neutral.

OpenOFDM WiFi real-file combined diagnostics148.51->158.65ms and query140.59->149.55ms: a small but real measured overhead, not a benefit. Fixed-source first-view hover remains about124ms in separate one-process public observations.
Large SoC background has expensive cold setup: Native2452ms versus combined47120ms (freeze48002ms); first edit also slower. Warm gains do not erase these setup costs.

Large SoC background kernel lifetime peak footprint: Native1737.6MiB, freeze5900.1MiB, combined4296.3MiB. Retention is not universally memory-saving. These are sampled workload maxima, not memory ceilings.
SPI/PSS real-file freeze-only warm response is better than combined; extra local-proof work does not always repay its cost.
Manual rebuild command alone is not complete rebuild latency; active-instance selection between command and post-rebuild edit is untimed.
Recommend opt-in based on workload: keep default off, disclose scope selections and Native boundaries, and preserve all first/warm/fallback/memory figures.

recommendations: Keep the feature opt-in. Prefer long editing sessions with stable RTL/library providers and repeated eligible function/task body edits.
Use actual selectors and observed imported roots when judging benefit. Large SoC real-edit measurements here freeze packages only.
For tested small RTL original-file cases expect near-neutral response; for OpenOFDM WiFi original-file edits expect the recorded small regression.
SPI/PSS real-edit can respond faster with freeze-only than combined local certification; choose by measured workload.

Next performance opportunities are expensive first-generation preparation, retained-owner memory and fixed-source first-query views. These remain explicit costs, not hidden claims of completed optimization.
